title: The Hobbit
author: J.R.R. Tolkien
description: Bilbo Baggins is swept from his comfortable hobbit-hole into an adventure with thirteen dwarves and a wizard, bound for a mountain guarded by a dragon.

reviews.name: Maya R.
reviews.text: Warm, funny, and adventurous. It still feels like the perfect doorway into fantasy.

reviews.name: Eli T.
reviews.text: The songs slowed me down at first, but Bilbo's growth won me over completely.

reviews.name: Jordan K.
reviews.text: A wonderfully cozy quest with just the right amount of danger.

title: Circe
author: Madeline Miller
description: In the house of Helios, god of the sun and mightiest of the Titans, a daughter is born. But Circe is a strange child--not powerful, like her father, nor viciously alluring like her mother.

reviews.name: Nina P.
reviews.text: There’s nothing I love more than a book by a woman about a woman, so Circe certainly fits the bill.

reviews.name: Cam B.
reviews.text: This is the pièce de résistance I’ve been searching for my entire life. Not only did I fall in love with this story, I predict that this will be the best book I’ll read all year. This book is about healing and doing what it takes to come into your own.

reviews.name: Renee S.
reviews.text: This was one of the most amazing, beautiful, intricate, captivating books I have had the pleasure of reading in my entire life.

title: Project Hail Mary
author: Andy Weir
description: A lone astronaut wakes without his memories and must solve an impossible scientific mystery to give humanity one last chance.

reviews.name: Andre L.
reviews.text: Big science, bigger heart. The central friendship made this one special.

reviews.name: Sam D.
reviews.text: Every chapter ends with a new problem, and somehow the solutions stay fun.

reviews.name: Priya N.
reviews.text: Some technical passages are dense, but the payoff is absolutely worth it.

title: The Thursday Murder Club
author: Richard Osman
description: Four clever residents of a retirement village meet weekly to investigate cold cases—until a real murder arrives on their doorstep.

reviews.name: Owen F.
reviews.text: Charming, twisty, and full of characters I would happily visit again.

reviews.name: Lou A.
reviews.text: The humor is gentle, but the mystery still has real bite.

reviews.name: Dani C.
reviews.text: A cozy mystery with a surprisingly moving view of friendship and age.

title: Educated
author: Tara Westover
description: A woman raised in an isolated survivalist family recounts how education opened a path toward knowledge, independence, and a new understanding of home.

reviews.name: Tess W.
reviews.text: A difficult, clear-eyed memoir about the cost of becoming your own person.

reviews.name: Marcus H.
reviews.text: Intense and beautifully written. I had to pause often to absorb it.

reviews.name: Jo V.
reviews.text: Her account of learning to trust her own memory is unforgettable.

title: The Midnight Library
author: Matt Haig
description: Between life and death stands a library filled with alternate lives, offering Nora Seed the chance to discover what makes a life worth living.

reviews.name: Avery M.
reviews.text: A hopeful and accessible story about regret, choice, and small joys.

reviews.name: Keisha G.
reviews.text: The premise is simple, but several of Nora's possible lives really stayed with me.

reviews.name: Ben I.
reviews.text: A little direct with its message, though ultimately comforting.

title: Becoming
author: Michelle Obama
description: Michelle Obama reflects on her childhood, career, family, and years in the White House with candor, warmth, and an invitation to keep becoming.

reviews.name: Imani J.
reviews.text: Thoughtful and personal, especially when she writes about ambition and family.

reviews.name: Chris E.
reviews.text: The Chicago chapters were my favorite—grounded, vivid, and generous.

reviews.name: Fatima Q.
reviews.text: It feels less like a victory lap and more like an honest conversation.

title: The Song of Achilles
author: Madeline Miller
description: Patroclus recounts his bond with the legendary Achilles, from their youth together to the glory and tragedy awaiting them at Troy.

reviews.name: Sofia R.
reviews.text: Lyrical, romantic, and devastating even when you already know the ending.

reviews.name: Theo P.
reviews.text: The mythology feels immediate because the emotional center is so human.

reviews.name: June C.
reviews.text: Miller made an ancient story feel startlingly intimate.
